Project decision / proposed assumption: What is this prototype release authorized to do?
Recommended option: Approve offline-only, non-operational solver comparison; explicitly exclude operational planning/release.
Alternatives: Planning support with human authority; operational control under separate railway authority program.
Consequences: Offline scope permits controlled experiments only. Broader scope requires new external authority, evidence, and assurance work.
Dependencies: Task 13 Decision B; Task 14 scope; no external railway authority implied.
Must resolve before implementation: Decision approved for bounded offline work; separate approval of the Task 16 implementation plan is required before source changes.

Project decision / proposed assumption: Which infrastructure registry/version defines physical segments, lines, routes and assets?
Recommended option: External infrastructure owner must identify and approve registry/version; no project-team substitute.
Alternatives: Adopt existing registry; establish governed registry; or leave topology-dependent claims blocked.
Consequences: No approved topology means the project cannot make real infrastructure conflict claims.
Dependencies: Infrastructure authority decision, versioned registry and mapping.

Project decision / proposed assumption: How are logical adjacency, junctions, crossovers and shared conflict resources defined?
Recommended option: External infrastructure/operations/safety owners define and approve relations; no inference from labels.
Alternatives: Versioned adjacency graph; activity-specific conflict matrix; or no operational adjacency model.
Consequences: Incorrect relations can omit or invent conflicts; current two-line model is only a simulation.
Dependencies: D-02 topology; approved relation semantics.

Project decision / proposed assumption: Which calibrated geometry/chainage and uncertainty define work and train footprints?
Recommended option: Infrastructure/data-governance owners approve coordinate reference and accuracy; otherwise spatial checks remain unknown.
Alternatives: Authoritative chainage; approved geospatial CRS; or no spatial pass.
Consequences: Current interpolated coordinates cannot support actual distance conclusions.
Dependencies: Versioned registry, calibration/uncertainty policy.

Project decision / proposed assumption: Which activity/equipment clearances and measurement boundaries apply?
Recommended option: Railway safety/infrastructure/maintenance authorities approve values and method; do not adopt prototype constants.
Alternatives: Activity-specific approved parameters; authenticated external rule provider; or remain unresolved.
Consequences: No numerical clearance is approved by Task 15; current constants cannot become policy by implementation.
Dependencies: D-04 geometry and approved safety basis.
Must resolve before implementation: Yes for any real clearance rule

Project decision / proposed assumption: Which provider is authoritative for movements and timetable scope?
Recommended option: Operations/data governance identify authenticated provider or governed versioned source; else use only fixed simulation snapshot.
Alternatives: Authenticated feed; governed signed export; or no operational feed.
Consequences: Bundled CSV presence does not establish authority/currentness/completeness.
Dependencies: Provider contract, identity/trust and allowed use.

Project decision / proposed assumption: What evidence establishes timetable completeness and freshness?
Recommended option: Provider and operations/safety owners define signed scope, validity and update protocol; otherwise UNKNOWN.
Alternatives: Authenticated completeness attestation; independently reconciled process; or no pass on absence.
Consequences: Without completeness evidence, absence of listed trains cannot pass verifier.
Dependencies: D-06 provider and evidence authentication.

Project decision / proposed assumption: What operating-date/time-zone/service-day semantics apply?
Recommended option: Operations/timetable owner approves date, named zone, overnight and calendar rules; else retain hour-based simulation only.
Alternatives: Absolute instants plus zone/calendar; approved railway operating-day convention; or reject date-ambiguous inputs.
Consequences: Current hour-of-day windows do not identify dated movements.
Dependencies: D-06 source and operating calendar.

Project decision / proposed assumption: How do timetable updates, cancellations and diversions affect schedules?
Recommended option: Operations/provider/safety owners approve update, freshness, revocation and invalidation lifecycle.
Alternatives: Ordered update stream; polling plus mandatory revalidation; or expire outputs and require review.
Consequences: No current mechanism can keep a prior schedule current after source changes.
Dependencies: D-06/07 provider protocol and schedule lifecycle.

Project decision / proposed assumption: Which work requires possession/closure and who authorizes it?
Recommended option: Railway operations authority defines activity requirements and granting authority; solver interval is never a grant.
Alternatives: Authority workflow integration; authenticated grant records; or proposal-only system.
Consequences: No operational release can be inferred from scheduled time.
Dependencies: Authority-owned procedure, scope, status and evidence.

Project decision / proposed assumption: What traction assets/isolation scope and confirmation authority apply?
Recommended option: Electrical/traction authority defines requirements and authenticated confirmation; absent provider remains UNKNOWN.
Alternatives: Authenticated scoped record; verifiable approval workflow; or no verified traction work.
Consequences: Boolean/source labels cannot demonstrate electrical isolation.
Dependencies: Electrical asset model and provider/trust protocol.

Project decision / proposed assumption: What worksite protection arrangements/evidence apply by task?
Recommended option: Operations/safety authority supplies approved requirements and evidence; software team must not invent procedures.
Alternatives: Authority rule catalogue; external protection-plan record; or verification blocked.
Consequences: No protection requirements are established in the current repository.
Dependencies: Task taxonomy and authorized protection evidence.

Project decision / proposed assumption: Which task taxonomy maps work types to qualifications, equipment and controls?
Recommended option: Maintenance/safety owners approve a controlled catalogue or identify an authoritative system; unknown types do not default permissively.
Alternatives: Versioned catalogue; authoritative work-order platform; or reject/unknown unsupported work.
Consequences: Free-text defect labels and department enums do not encode task requirements.
Dependencies: Task catalog, owners and rule mapping.

Project decision / proposed assumption: How should synthetic urgency trade against aggregate coverage in research?
Recommended option: For the existing-model comparison, preserve generated urgency only as an input/search-order field; report per-urgency outcomes descriptively, not as approved priority.
Alternatives: Synthetic lexicographic priority tiers; total count first then urgency; omit urgency from comparisons.
Consequences: Any policy changes selected work and invalidates direct comparison with historical outcomes; no choice establishes operational priority.
Dependencies: D-01; frozen task instances; separate benchmark configuration.
Must resolve before implementation: Yes before adding or interpreting urgency as an objective

Project decision / proposed assumption: Which objective hierarchy and quality claims will research use?
Recommended option: Keep hard modeled constraints separate; report coverage first, then current objective components individually; do not combine solver-specific scaled values into an equivalence claim.
Alternatives: Approved lexicographic research objective; Pareto reporting; weighted objective with sensitivity analysis.
Consequences: Current baseline and CP-SAT objectives differ in coverage priority/scaling and baseline lacks optimality proof. Any new common objective requires a separate implementation and validation task.
Dependencies: D-01; model crosswalk; independent objective evaluator before objective-quality comparison.
Must resolve before implementation: Decision approved: present validated hard-constraint status, coverage and proof state first, then current objective components separately; independent evaluation remains required before objective-quality claims.

Project decision / proposed assumption: What proxy, if any, represents disruption in offline experiments?
Recommended option: Retain current time-of-day/train-gap term only under its exact code name and label it a prototype heuristic, not delay/disruption cost.
Alternatives: Omit the term from cross-solver objective comparisons; introduce synthetic disruption penalties.
Consequences: Keeping it supports historical reproduction only; a synthetic replacement changes model results and must be stated.
Dependencies: D-01; fixed timetable snapshot; solver objective description.
Must resolve before implementation: Yes before presenting it as a research metric

Project decision / proposed assumption: May generic crew capacity be tested using artificial data?
Recommended option: Allow only isolated synthetic fixtures with generated crew IDs and artificial availability/qualification tags; do not assert staff feasibility.
Alternatives: Defer all crew constraints; seek real governed roster in a separate external approval process.
Consequences: Synthetic fixtures test solver mechanics only and cannot demonstrate qualified personnel or legal compliance.
Dependencies: D-01; fixture labeling; a separately approved constraint implementation and independent validator.
Must resolve before implementation: Yes before adding synthetic crew fixtures

Project decision / proposed assumption: May generic equipment capacity/compatibility be tested using artificial data?
Recommended option: Allow artificial equipment type/count/capacity fixtures only, clearly separate from `heavy_equipment` and actual assets.
Alternatives: Keep equipment out of model; request authoritative inventory for any operational claim.
Consequences: Synthetic test can exercise cumulative resource constraints but has no equipment-feasibility value for railway operations.
Dependencies: D-01; fixture schema; independent resource validator; future solver adapters.

Project decision / proposed assumption: May generic travel/setup transitions be tested?
Recommended option: Use only explicitly generated transition matrices in synthetic fixtures; do not infer travel from route/section IDs.
Alternatives: Omit transitions; provide validated network/time data under a future external approval.
Consequences: Synthetic transition results test algorithm response only and cannot describe actual access or travel.
Dependencies: D-01; D-17/D-18 fixtures if resources move; no operational route claims.

Project decision / proposed assumption: Which shift, duty, break, maximum-work and rest policies apply?
Recommended option: External workforce/maintenance/safety authority must approve policy and data; objective buckets are not rules.
Alternatives: Approved policy engine; authoritative roster calendars; otherwise leave crew feasibility unknown.
Consequences: No project-team decision can establish legal or railway duty/rest requirements.
Dependencies: Policy source, roster/history and applicability.

Project decision / proposed assumption: How should duration uncertainty and interruption be represented experimentally?
Recommended option: For historical reproduction, retain fixed generated `duration_hrs`; test alternate distributions/splits only as separate synthetic scenarios.
Alternatives: Use synthetic conservative margin; add multi-phase robust-duration scenarios; keep all durations fixed.
Consequences: Separate variants are not comparable to historical Task 12 unless clearly versioned; no duration estimate is an actual maintenance estimate.
Dependencies: D-01; synthetic scenario generator approval; objective/model versioning.
Must resolve before implementation: Yes before adding alternative duration model

Project decision / proposed assumption: May synthetic work windows/deadlines be used in tests?
Recommended option: Allow illustrative windows and deadlines only in named synthetic scenarios; do not export them to default or custom real work orders.
Alternatives: Keep absent; use actual authoritative work-order/operations feed only after external approval.
Consequences: Artificial windows can validate constraint code but not an operational deadline or possession window.
Dependencies: D-01; fixture labeling; date/time semantics for simulation; independent validator.

Project decision / proposed assumption: May generic precedence dependencies be tested?
Recommended option: Allow synthetic dependency DAGs and lags only for algorithm tests; reject/flag cycles in fixtures and make no engineering-sequence claim.
Alternatives: Keep dependencies out; later obtain authoritative work-order relations.
Consequences: Synthetic graph validates precedence implementation, not actual maintenance sequencing.
Dependencies: D-01; explicit synthetic graph schema and validation cases.

Project decision / proposed assumption: How is current exact-window co-location treated in experiments?
Recommended option: Preserve current bilateral Boolean/exact-window behavior only as a named legacy simulation assumption; do not call it approved co-location.
Alternatives: Disable co-location in future comparative instances; use a separate synthetic shared-access model.
Consequences: Changing policy can alter coverage and objectives. Current flag lacks shared-site, crew, equipment, possession, and protection evidence.
Dependencies: D-01; fixed model version; any changed rule needs independent validation.

Project decision / proposed assumption: How should solver outcome, proof state, partial output, and safety state be communicated in research?
Recommended option: Report coverage state, termination reason, proof flags, and evidence verification as separate fields; preserve backend behavior in this documentation-only proposal.
Alternatives: A single enum with explicit precedence and metadata; defer operator UI/API semantics.
Consequences: Separate dimensions avoid equating a limit with infeasibility or solver success with safety. Does not authorize an API change.
Dependencies: D-01; solver-specific outcome mapping; Task 13 discrepancy disclosure.
Must resolve before implementation: Decision approved for research reporting; no production API or safety-verifier change is authorized.

Project decision / proposed assumption: What evidence states, applicability, audit denominator, retention and revocation semantics are required?
Recommended option: Railway safety/data governance owners approve semantics; preserve current fail-closed behavior until then.
Alternatives: Explicit four-state audit; rigorously specified legacy bool/null contract; otherwise no verified-status claim.
Consequences: Changing verified status/compliance semantics affects the safety boundary and evidence retention.
Dependencies: D-10/11/12 evidence sources and governance policy.

Project decision / proposed assumption: What retention, privacy, security, access and audit requirements govern real timetable/workforce/safety data?
Recommended option: Obtain data-governance/security/railway approval before ingesting or persisting such data.
Alternatives: Apply existing authority policy; create an approved project-specific policy; otherwise use public/synthetic data only.
Consequences: Project permission is not a substitute for data rights or governance.
Dependencies: Data classification, access controls, retention and audit policy.

Project decision / proposed assumption: What changes invalidate schedules and who can re-authorize them?
Recommended option: Operations/safety/data governance approve invalidation and reauthorization lifecycle; do not claim current schedule validity in offline scope.
Alternatives: Invalidate on relevant source change; impact analysis with human review; expiry and mandatory refresh.
Consequences: Current project has no schedule lifecycle or update authority.
Dependencies: D-09 feed lifecycle, evidence revocation and operational authority.
Must resolve before implementation: Yes before schedule reuse or release

Project decision / proposed assumption: What evidence is required before making optimization/coverage proof claims?
Recommended option: Use only solver-provided proof for the exact encoded model; distinguish complete incumbent, coverage proof, objective proof, and no proof.
Alternatives: Report bounds/gaps where available; omit optimality claims without proof.
Consequences: CP-SAT proof applies to its scaled model; baseline has no global objective certificate. No proof implies no optimality claim.
Dependencies: D-01; capture termination/proof metadata; independent model validation.
Must resolve before implementation: Decision approved: claims remain scoped to exact-model proof metadata; independent validation and proof-state capture are implementation prerequisites.

Project decision / proposed assumption: Which data/distributions may be used for bounded benchmark work?
Recommended option: Use bundled `IRCTC_cleaned.csv` only as a frozen non-authoritative input snapshot and current deterministic generated orders only as synthetic; cap experiments at available orders unless new synthetic generator is separately approved.
Alternatives: Generate larger synthetic workloads; use governed anonymized operational data only after explicit data-governance approval.
Consequences: Current data support only narrow synthetic/historical claims. Larger generated workloads are not observed operations; governed data requires separate rights/security review.
Dependencies: D-01; record file digest, parser version, random seed, instance digest and workload size.
Must resolve before implementation: Yes before interpreting benchmark scope beyond existing inputs
